title: Process scripts: one cross-platform implementation for gate, collect-decisions and release (Windows, macOS, Linux)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-10): "the quick gate and other powershell scripts should be generic for mac, linux and windows."

## Today
- **`scripts/gate.ps1` (268 lines) and `scripts/gate.sh` (174 lines) are two hand-kept twins.** They have already drifted: `gate.sh`'s quick tier runs every suite of a touched crate, while `gate.ps1` narrows to the changed `#[test]` fns. Their CLIs differ (`-Tier quick` / `-Test <name>` against `quick` / `test <name>`), and `SLOW_BINARIES` is kept "in step" by hand.
- **`scripts/collect-decisions.ps1` / `.sh`** are another pair.
- **`scripts/release.ps1`** (the cut: release gate, version bump, zip, installer) has no macOS/Linux twin, so a cut can only run on Windows.
- **Windows assumptions in AGENTS.md:** it names only `gate.ps1` (`-Tier quick`, `-Test <name>`), `release.ps1` and `collect-decisions.ps1`, and the agents and skills follow it. So an agent on macOS or Linux gets Windows instructions.
- **Platform-bound by nature:** `sign.ps1` and `installer.ps1` (Windows signing and installer) and `package-*.sh` (per-OS packaging) are correctly tied to their platform and stay that way.

## Proposal (recommended): `cargo xtask`
Move the logic of `gate`, `collect-decisions` and the platform-neutral half of `release` into a small Rust `xtask` crate in the workspace (`cargo xtask gate quick`, `cargo xtask gate test <name>`, `cargo xtask decisions --version X.Y.Z`, `cargo xtask release --version X.Y.Z --no-tag`).
- Cargo is already on every contributor's machine, so it needs no PowerShell 7 on macOS/Linux and no bash on Windows. It is one implementation, so it can't drift.
- The diff-to-suite mapping (the gate maps in the suite headers), `SLOW_BINARIES` and the tiers live once, in Rust, with unit tests.
- Test executables come from cargo's JSON artifact list, never a `*.exe` glob (the glob once launched the GUI).
- `scripts/gate.ps1` / `gate.sh` become 3-line wrappers that call `cargo xtask gate "$@"`, so muscle memory and fork process-sync keep working.
- The packaging steps `release` calls stay per platform (`installer.ps1`/`sign.ps1` on Windows, `package-*.sh` elsewhere), and the release refuses by name a step its OS can't run.

Alternative considered: one PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) script for all three OSes. It is simpler to port, but it makes every macOS/Linux contributor install pwsh. Two twins kept in step by review is today's state and has already drifted.

## Process follow-ups (same PR or right after)
- AGENTS.md "Three gate tiers", "Test the change", the release steps and the process-file list name the cross-platform command (and `xtask/` joins the process files the fork sync pulls). PROCESS_VERSION bump, announced on #681.
- The skills and agents that call the gate (`gate-runner`, `PR-reviewer`, `review-prs`, `resolve-conflicts`, `work-issue` from #747) switch to the one command.

## Done means
- `cargo xtask gate quick|batch|release|test <name>` runs the same plan on Windows, macOS and Linux. A unit test pins the diff-to-suite selection and the slow-binary list, and a `DRY_RUN`/`--plan` mode prints the plan without running.
- `cargo xtask decisions` and `cargo xtask release --no-tag` work on all three OSes. Platform-only packaging steps are called per OS or refused by name.
- `gate.ps1` / `gate.sh` / `collect-decisions.*` are thin wrappers (or removed), and AGENTS.md and the skills name one command.
